metaTitle: The page's <title> and the title of link previews. Keep "Kando" in Latin letters.
metaDescription: Meta description for search results and link previews, about 150 to 200 characters in English; keep it to one or two sentences.
metaImageAlt: Description of the preview image (the library screenshot) for link previews.
skipToContent: Link for keyboard and screen reader users that jumps past the header to the page's content; visible only when focused.
homeLabel: Accessible name of the Kando logo in the header and footer, which links to the top of this page.
navLabel: Accessible name of the header's list of section links.
navHowItWorks: Header link to the How it works section. Keep it short: the header has little room.
navFeatures: Header link to the Features section.
navGetStarted: Header link to the Get started section.
languageLabel: Accessible name of the language switcher in the header and of the footer's list of languages. The languages themselves are always named in their own language and are not translated.
githubLabel: Accessible name of the GitHub icon in the header.
heroEyebrow: Small pill above the headline. "MIT" is the license's name and stays as is.
heroTitle: The headline. The app's own description is "a desktop app for learning a language from videos in that language": keep that meaning, and write it as a natural headline rather than a literal translation.
heroLead: One or two sentences under the headline: what Kando does with a video, in the order it happens.
heroDownload: Primary button, links to GitHub Releases.
heroSource: Secondary button, links to the repository on GitHub.
heroReleaseNote: Under the buttons. No release exists yet, so the Download button leads to an empty Releases page: this says so. Followed by the link heroBuildLink.
heroBuildLink: Link after heroReleaseNote to the Build from source card further down.
heroPlatforms: Operating systems Kando builds for. Keep the names in Latin letters; the separator may follow your language's convention.
heroAudioNote: Next to heroPlatforms: audio playback works only on macOS; on Windows and Linux the player shows the picture without sound.
shotLibraryAlt: Alt text of the hero screenshot of the library. The README in your language has the same text as its first picture's description; reuse it.
howTitle: Heading of the How it works section.
howLead: Line under the heading: jobs run one after another, and a failed job says why and links to the setting that fixes it.
stepAddTitle: Step 1 title, a short verb phrase.
stepAddBody: Step 1: paste a link or drop a video file. mp4, mov, mkv and webm are file formats and stay as is.
stepDownloadBody: Step 2: yt-dlp is a program's name and is written in lower case, even at the start of a sentence.
stepTranscribeBody: Step 3: whisper.cpp is a program's name and is written in lower case. The point is that it runs on the reader's own computer.
stepTranslateBody: Step 4: "OpenAI-compatible" means any service with the same API as OpenAI; use the term the app's AI Service settings use in your language.
stepWatchBody: Step 5: .srt is the SubRip subtitle file format and stays as is.
featuresLead: Line under the heading. "Go" is the programming language.
featureOnDeviceTitle: Feature card title: speech recognition runs locally.
featureOnDeviceBody: Settings › Speech Recognition is the app's menu path: use the exact wording of the app's interface in your language (apps/kando/locales). Keep the model names Tiny and Large v3 and the sizes as they are.
featureModelTitle: Feature card title: the reader chooses which AI model translates.
featureModelBody: EveryAPI and the provider names are product names and stay as is, except where the app itself names them differently in your language (for example Qwen, Kimi, Zhipu GLM).
featureModelLink: Link to everyapi.ai under the card.
featurePlayerTitle: Feature card title about the player that shows both languages.
featurePlayerBody: Subtitle modes as the player offers them: both lines, original only, translation only, off. Use the app's wording for them where it fits.
featureFoldersTitle: Feature card title: a library is an ordinary folder.
featureFoldersBody: .kando and .srt stay as is. Finder is the macOS file manager's name; use the name Apple uses in your language.
featureSitesTitle: Feature card title. {count} is the number of sites in the catalog, such as 929.
featureSitesBody: Help › Supported Websites… is the app's menu path: use the exact wording of the app's interface in your language.
sitesStripLabel: Accessible name of the row of site logos.
sitesMore: After the row of logos. {count} is how many more sites the catalog lists, such as 894.
featureLanguagesTitle: Feature card title: the app's interface comes in five languages.
featureLanguagesBody: Names the five interface languages in your language. Settings › General is the app's menu path in your language.
featureUploadTitle: Feature card title: uploading is optional and goes to the reader's own storage.
featureUploadBody: Cloud storage names follow the provider's own name in your language where it has one (for example 阿里云 OSS, 腾讯云 COS).
featureShortcutsBody: ⌘/ is the shortcut that opens the cheat sheet and stays as is. Settings › Keyboard Shortcuts is the app's menu path in your language.
playerTitle: Heading of the dark section showing the player screenshot.
shotPlayerAlt: Alt text of the player screenshot; the README in your language has it as the second picture's description.
settingsTitle: Heading of the section with two Settings screenshots.
settingsGeneralCaption: Caption under the Settings › General screenshot. "General" is the section's name in the app.
shotSettingsGeneralAlt: Alt text of the Settings › General screenshot; the README in your language has it.
settingsAICaption: Caption under the Settings › AI Service screenshot. AI Service and Test Connection are names in the app: use the app's wording.
shotSettingsAIAlt: Alt text of the Settings › AI Service screenshot; the README in your language has it.
startTitle: Heading of the Get started section, also the header's last link target.
startDownloadBody: No version has been published yet; builds will be attached to GitHub Releases. Do not promise a date.
startDownloadUnsigned: Smaller text: the builds are not code-signed, so the system warns on first launch. Developer ID is Apple's term and stays as is.
startDownloadButton: Button in card 1 linking to GitHub Releases.
startToolsBody: Kando uses these programs but does not install or update them.
toolYtdlp: What yt-dlp is for, written as a short phrase after the program's name in a two-column list.
toolFfmpeg: What ffmpeg is for, a short phrase.
toolWhisper: What whisper-cli is for, a short phrase. whisper.cpp is the project's name and stays as is.
startToolsMac: Line before the brew command. Homebrew stays as is.
startToolsOther: PATH is the environment variable and stays as is.
startToolsAudio: Audio works only on macOS for now; state it plainly.
startBuildBody: Line before the build commands. Go is the programming language; keep the version number.
startBuildNote: make build is a command and stays as is, as do apps/kando/build, Kando.app and .dmg. ad-hoc signed is a code-signing term.
startReadme: Link under the cards to the README in your language.
copyLabel: Button next to a command that copies it.
copiedLabel: The copy button's label for a moment after it copied.
footerTagline: One line under the logo in the footer, the same idea as heroTitle as a plain sentence.
footerLicense: Footer link to the LICENSE file. MIT stays as is.
footerLinksLabel: Accessible name of the footer's list of project links.
footerGitHub: Footer link to the repository. GitHub stays as is.
footerReleases: Footer link to GitHub Releases. Use the name GitHub uses in your language, or keep Releases.
footerReadme: Footer link to the README in your language. README stays as is.
notFoundTitle: Heading of the 404 page. One 404 page serves every missing address, so it shows this text in English first and then in every other language with its link home.
notFoundHome: Button on the 404 page back to the home page.
